headline: PINBALL gets a TABLE SMITH — build your own cabinet
lede: The arcade now ships a construction set: three years of shared-engine work (#3103) become playable — a player-built cabinet is data, not physics. The third attract card opens a pad-first bench; your named machine rides the row, plays itself in the demo, and survives a reload.

notes.text: TABLE SMITH (#3284): arrows walk a cursor, A places, B cycles 8 tools (bumper/sling/bank/magnet/wipe/name/test/save). TEST drops one ball and comes home to the bench; SAVE names it and the cabinet joins the row for real — same 240 Hz physics, same scoring ladder, kit-dressable.

Legality is zones, not vibes: dome-ellipse clamps, a 60 px flipper corridor held by the sling anchors, and the cursor ghost runs the compiler's own law — green commits, red refuses with a named reason.
pinballcheck 206/206 with two new mutants caught (9/9); new pinballsmith live drive 22/22 real-key legs; pinballplay 54/54 after re-cutting one hardcoded tap coord for the wider row.

Board hygiene: #3237's tail wording now word-matches its README gaps, so weakestStage sees it owns them — the pinball phantom score dropped 6 to 3 and the next kick lands on an honest gap (single-ball music bed).
